narr: During the late evening of the 25th and morning of the 26th, storms moved repeatedly along and north of an outflow boundary that extended along Interstate 44 from Lebanon to Joplin. Rainfall accumulations of over three inches occurred in a 12-hour period ending at 9 AM on the 26th along the Missouri-Kansas border from Fort Scott southward to Pittsburg, and from Joplin to Seneca. A Flash Flood Emergency was issued for Seneca when five to eight inches of rainfall in a four-hour period led to flooded homes and businesses along Lost Creek. Six vehicle water rescues were conducted, and 25 to 30 homes were evacuated as the water was rising. Widespread flooding of roads occurred throughout Newton and Jasper counties, including Highway 86 near Reddings Mill and Highway 37 east of Joplin.
ev: Highway CC at Lock Creek was flooded and impassable.
Highway 86 at Shoal Creek was flooded and impassable.
Water was reported over the road at Highway 43 and Iris Road making it impassable to traffic.

Evacuations of several homes along Lost Creek in the City of Seneca occurred as the creek rose rapidly out of its banks. Water was reported in basements and some businesses. No injuries were reported.
The bridge at the intersection of Martin and Elder Roads was reported as underwater as Carver Creek flowed out of its banks. .
Bethel Road south of Kentucky Road was washed out from heavy rainfall and flooding.
Excessive rainfall caused flooding on Spring and McCord Streets as Hickory Creek flowed out of its banks.
Route CC was closed at Lost Creek due to flooding.
Missouri Highway 37 at the Spring River was closed due to flooding.
Excessive rainfall caused Lost Creek to flow out of its banks flooding Oneida and Main Streets in town.
